text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.

-- Shareholders approve Eurotunnel financial restructuring plan, more than 95 percent of votes at meeting cast in favour of plan. Eurotunnel expects 1997 profit to be higher than initially forecast. (Les Echos, La Tribune, L'Agefi, Le Figaro, Liberation, The International Herald Tribune).
LES ECHOS
-- Government to take over a further 20 billion francs worth of debt from SNCF railroad operator, which in exchange commits itself to hiring some 2,000 people.

-- Public deficits for 1997 may reach 3.5 percent of GDP, according to a confidential note sent by Former Prime Minister Alain Juppe to his successor Lionel Jospin on June 2, citing a 35 billion franc undershooting in revenue and an eight billion francs overshooting in spending.
-- Arms manufacturer Giat Industries signs letter of intent to sell its 92 percent stake in Belgium's Herstal to U.S. group Colt's Manufacturing.
-- Credit Lyonnais workers reluctant to use third layoff plan which is to cut some 5,000 jobs to end 1998, notably through early retirements.
LA TRIBUNE
-- Lagardere considers selling radio stations Chante France and RFM to be allowed by audio visual regulatory authority CSA to develop other projects, notably the Europe 1 radio network.
-- Paris bourse recorded highest ever half yearly volume in the first six months of 1997, with transactions amounting to some 1,119 billion francs.
-- Former group Credit National-BFCE, Natexis, expects a return on shareholders' equity for 1998.
L'AGEFI
-- French current account reached a 20.3 billion francs surplus in April, its highest since 1945.
LE FIGARO-ECONOMIE
-- 98 percent of voting shareholders approve Eurotunnel financial restructuring plan.
LIBERATION (Economic section)
-- A reform of European agricultural policy worries unions.
THE INTERNATIONAL HERALD TRIBUNE
-- Eurotunnel holders vore for rescue plan.
